action: Check your email address on Have I Been Pwned. If it appears, change that password everywhere it was reused and turn on two-step sign-in.
exec: Old stolen credentials keep circulating; newly indexed leaks can trigger fresh account-takeover attempts.
plain: A breach-checking service added two old Russian data leaks, so millions of people can now see whether their email addresses and passwords were exposed.
summary: Have I Been Pwned catalogued a 2013 breach of the Russian-language cybercrime forum YouHack on November 11, covering 7.2 million unique email addresses. Only about 107,000 belonged to forum members; the rest were victims' credentials that members had posted. The same day it added a 2023 breach of Sberbank's SberSpasibo loyalty programme with 3.3 million unique emails.
title: Old breaches of Russian forum YouHack and Sberbank's SberSpasibo added to Have I Been Pwned

validation.note: One established outlet reporting the Have I Been Pwned additions.

review.note: Compared 11 Nov date, YouHack 2013 breach 7.2M emails with ~107,000 members, SberSpasibo 3.3M unique emails against The Register
